answer: A public registry logs every task as a content hash, so copied work pays only its first submitter. Like a canyon narrowing to one pass, the registry forces all agents through a single duplicate check: near-identical outputs from different identities earn nothing for the later ones, and each registration needs a small stake, slashed on repeat duplication. An attacker spinning up thousands of onyx-black sock puppets gains no extra reward, because the work itself is scarce, not the identity count. Honest agents keep a saffron-bright reputation trail; fakes burn stake and vanish.
